title: Service Account JWT claim identifiers, the key generation command and references to the key file
summary: A JWT claims payload holding the documented Organization ID, Technical Account ID and API key identifiers, the OpenSSL command that writes private.key and certificate_pub.crt, a reference to the key file by path in an environment assignment, and prose that names the public certificate.
rationale: The private key of the retired Service Account (JWT) credential is a locally generated signing key that is never uploaded, and the evidence names it by its role and its file name, not by an encoding or a marker. What sits beside it is not the key: the JWT payload carries the Organization ID, the Technical Account ID and the API key as identifiers in documented formats, the generation command and the path of private.key name the file without containing it, and the public certificate is the verification half that is uploaded to Adobe. Protecting these as the private key would redact the identifiers, command and file names a reader needs to understand which key a configuration refers to. The identifiers' own confidentiality is not stated by Adobe, so this Case asserts only that they are not the signing key, and the signed assertion derived from the key is a separate, unsettled Case.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#238, Group E). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the texts here are claim identifiers, a generation command, a file-path reference and a sentence about the public certificate, not the private signing key. Adobe documents the identifier formats, the command and the file names and the upload of the public certificate; that none of them is the key is a project decision, and no encoding, header label or length of the key is claimed.

sources.supports: iss is the Organization ID in the format org_ident@AdobeOrg, sub is the Technical Account ID in the format id@techacct.adobe.com and aud is the API key in the format https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/c/api_key; these are identifiers carried in the JWT payload, not the private key.
sources.locator: section "Required Claims for a Service Account JWT"

sources.supports: The developer generates the private key and public certificate locally with an OpenSSL command that writes the key to a file named private.key and the certificate to certificate_pub.crt, and uploads only the public certificate; the page states no encoding, prefix, header label or length for the private key file.
sources.locator: section "Create a Public Key Certificate", MacOS and Linux

sources.supports: The exchange request has three URL-encoded body parameters, client_id, client_secret and jwt_token (a base-64 encoded JSON Web Token signed with a private key); the table lists no parameter that carries the private key itself.
sources.locator: sections "Exchanging JWT to retrieve an access token" and "Request parameters"
